### How we work

- **NDA before discovery**: We sign a mutual NDA before any technical discussion. Your idea, data and roadmap stay confidential from the first call.
- **You own the code**: Source code, designs and IP transfer to you as milestones are paid. Work lives in repositories you control, not ours.
- **Least-privilege access**: Engineers get only the access a task needs. Credentials live in a secrets manager, never in chat or source code, and are revoked at handover.
- **Demo every two weeks**: Agile sprints with a working demo every two weeks, a shared board, and a single point of contact who answers within one business day.

### Engagement models

- **Fixed scope**: We agree scope, timeline and price up front, then deliver in milestones. Changes go through a lightweight change request. Best for: Well-defined MVPs and projects with a clear spec. Pricing basis: Fixed price per milestone.
- **Dedicated team**: A team of engineers, design and QA works only on your product, embedded in your tools and rituals. Scale up or down monthly. Best for: Ongoing product development and evolving roadmaps. Pricing basis: Monthly rate per team member.
- **Time & materials**: Pay for the hours worked, tracked transparently with weekly reports. Ideal when scope is still being discovered. Best for: Discovery, audits, prototypes and short engagements. Pricing basis: Hourly rate, billed monthly.

### Frequently asked questions

#### What types of businesses do you work with?

We work with startups, SMEs, and enterprises across industries including FinTech, HealthTech, E-Commerce, EdTech, and Logistics. If you have a problem that technology can solve, we can help.

#### How long does a typical project take?

Project timelines vary based on scope and complexity. An MVP typically takes 6–10 weeks. Full-scale enterprise platforms range from 3–6 months. We follow agile sprints with regular demos so you see progress every 2 weeks.

#### Do you provide post-launch support and maintenance?

Yes. We offer flexible support packages including bug fixes, performance monitoring, feature updates, and uptime monitoring with automated alerting. We treat every project as a long-term partnership.

#### What AI and ML technologies do you specialize in?

We specialize in LLMs (GPT, Gemini, Claude), computer vision, NLP, recommendation engines, predictive analytics, and custom ML pipelines. We build on PyTorch, TensorFlow, and cloud AI services from AWS, GCP, and Azure.

#### How do we get started with Hunexture?

Simply reach out via our contact form or WhatsApp. We start with a free 30-minute discovery call to understand your goals, followed by a detailed proposal within 48 hours. No commitment required.

#### Do you sign NDAs before project discussions?

Absolutely. We sign NDAs before any technical discussions. Your business ideas, data, and processes are treated with strict confidentiality throughout our engagement.

### How we work

- **NDA before discovery**: We sign a mutual NDA before any technical discussion. Your idea, data and roadmap stay confidential from the first call.
- **You own the code**: Source code, designs and IP transfer to you as milestones are paid. Work lives in repositories you control, not ours.
- **Least-privilege access**: Engineers get only the access a task needs. Credentials live in a secrets manager, never in chat or source code, and are revoked at handover.
- **Demo every two weeks**: Agile sprints with a working demo every two weeks, a shared board, and a single point of contact who answers within one business day.

#### How do we get started with Hunexture?

Simply reach out via our contact form or WhatsApp. We start with a free 30-minute discovery call to understand your goals, followed by a detailed proposal within 48 hours. No commitment required.

#### How long does a typical project take?

Project timelines vary based on scope and complexity. An MVP typically takes 6–10 weeks. Full-scale enterprise platforms range from 3–6 months. We follow agile sprints with regular demos so you see progress every 2 weeks.

### Engagement models

- **Fixed scope**: We agree scope, timeline and price up front, then deliver in milestones. Changes go through a lightweight change request. Best for: Well-defined MVPs and projects with a clear spec. Pricing basis: Fixed price per milestone.
- **Dedicated team**: A team of engineers, design and QA works only on your product, embedded in your tools and rituals. Scale up or down monthly. Best for: Ongoing product development and evolving roadmaps. Pricing basis: Monthly rate per team member.
- **Time & materials**: Pay for the hours worked, tracked transparently with weekly reports. Ideal when scope is still being discovered. Best for: Discovery, audits, prototypes and short engagements. Pricing basis: Hourly rate, billed monthly.

### Security and confidentiality

We follow secure-by-default engineering: encrypted data in transit and at rest, environment separation between development and production, peer-reviewed pull requests, dependency scanning in CI, and documented handover. We do not use client data to train models outside your project. Where your industry requires it (HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS), we design to those requirements and work alongside your compliance team — we do not claim certifications we do not hold.

## AI Solutions

> Transform your business with cutting-edge artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions. We develop custom AI models tailored to your specific…

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/services/ai-solutions/

### Overview

Transform your business with cutting-edge artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions. We develop custom AI models tailored to your specific needs, from predictive analytics to computer vision applications.

### Key features

- Machine Learning
- Neural Networks
- Predictive Analytics
- Computer Vision

### Benefits

- Automate complex decision-making processes
- Gain insights from vast amounts of data
- Improve accuracy and efficiency
- Scale intelligent automation across your organization

### How we work

- **1. Discovery & Analysis**: We analyze your data and business requirements to identify AI opportunities
- **2. Model Development**: Our experts build and train custom ML models using state-of-the-art algorithms
- **3. Testing & Validation**: Rigorous testing ensures accuracy and reliability before deployment
- **4. Deployment & Monitoring**: We deploy your AI solution and continuously monitor performance

### Technologies

- OpenAI
- Codex
- Vertex AI
- Cloud Vision
- OpenCV
- TensorFlow
- IBM Watson
- Cloud Natural Language
- Cognitive Services
- Bot Framework
- Mistral
- Meta Llama
- Gemini
- Anthropic
- N8N

### Use cases

- **Predictive Maintenance**: Forecast equipment failures before they happen, reducing downtime and costs
- **Intelligent Automation**: Automate repetitive tasks with AI-powered decision making
- **Image Recognition**: Identify objects, faces, and patterns in images and videos
- **Natural Language Processing**: Extract insights from text, enable chatbots, and automate document processing

### Frequently asked questions

#### How long does it take to develop an AI solution?

Timeline varies based on complexity, but typical projects range from 2-6 months including data preparation, model development, and deployment.

#### Do I need a large dataset?

While more data generally improves accuracy, we can work with various dataset sizes and use techniques like transfer learning and data augmentation.

#### How do you ensure AI model accuracy?

We use rigorous testing methodologies, cross-validation, and continuous monitoring to maintain high accuracy levels.

- **High-speed Similarity Search**: Querying millions of embeddings in milliseconds.

Technologies: Pinecone, Redis, Elasticsearch

- **Cloud Agnostic**: Avoid vendor lock-in with portable, containerized architectures.
- **FinOps Obsessed**: AI compute is expensive; we architect specifically to minimize idle GPU costs.
- **Security Hardened**: VPC peering and strict RBAC tailored for proprietary datasets.

- **Orchestration**: Kubernetes, Docker, Helm
- **ML Lifecycle**: MLflow, Kubeflow, Weights & Biases

- **Design (2 weeks)**: Choose components and write the architecture.
- **Build (4 to 10 weeks)**: Provision, deploy and migrate the first workloads.
- **Operate (Ongoing)**: Capacity, cost and upgrades.

### Risks and controls

- **GPU cost overruns**: Right-sizing, spot capacity and scale-to-zero serving.
- **Vendor lock-in**: Open standards and portable containers.
- **Security gaps**: Network isolation, secrets management and audit logs.

### Frequently asked questions

Cloud is faster to start. On-premises or private cloud makes sense for steady heavy load or strict data rules. We cost both.

Not for many workloads. Hosted model APIs and small models run without them. We size to your actual usage.

> Move beyond passive prompts. Hunexture builds AI Agents capable of formulating plans, iterating through obstacles, and utilizing external software tools…

### Overview

Autonomous Digital Digital Workers executing multi-step workflows. Move beyond passive prompts. Hunexture builds AI Agents capable of formulating plans, iterating through obstacles, and utilizing external software tools (like APIs, browsers, and terminals) to accomplish complex objectives without human intervention.

### What we offer

#### Custom Tool Integration

Wiring agents to interact securely with your existing SaaS and internal systems.

- **REST/GraphQL API usage**: Agents that can read Swagger files and execute API calls.
- **Browser Manipulation**: Navigating legacy websites to scrape data or submit forms.
- **Database Queries**: Agents granted read-access to internal SQL tables.

#### Multi-Agent Collaborative Systems

Deploying swarms of specialized agents that talk to each other to solve grand challenges.

- **Role Delegation**: A "Manager" agent dividing work among "Research" and "Writer" agents.
- **Iterative Peer Review**: Agent A writes code, Agent B reviews it, Agent A corrects it.
- **Shared Memory Layers**: Agents maintaining common context across long-running tasks.

Technologies: AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph

#### Guardrails & Human-in-the-Loop

Ensuring autonomous agents never perform destructive actions without consent.

- **Execution Pauses**: Halting workflow to wait for a human "Approve" click before API mutations.
- **Semantic Routing**: Blocking agents from discussing or operating outside their defined scope.
- **Comprehensive Auditing**: Logging the exact "thought process" of the agent for compliance.

Technologies: NeMo Guardrails, LangSmith, PromptShield

### Why Hunexture

- **Production Reliability**: We transition fragile script-based agents into robust fault-tolerant systems.
- **Advanced State Management**: Engineering long-term episodic memory for agents via advanced vector topologies.
- **Security Forefront**: Limiting agent blast-radius via scoped ephemeral environments.
- **Deterministic Fallbacks**: Combining rigid classical programming with probabilistic LLM reasoning.

### Technologies

- **Agent Frameworks**: LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, BabyAGI
- **Tooling**: OpenAI Tool Calling, SERP APIs
- **Memory**: Zep, Mem0, Redis
- **Evaluation**: LangSmith, TruLens

### Outcome

Agents that complete multi-step tasks through your tools, inside limits you set and with a full record of every step.

### Best for

- Support, operations or back-office work with clear rules
- Tasks that today need several clicks across systems
- Teams ready to start with drafts and widen autonomy over time

### Deliverables

- Tool definitions with scopes and limits
- Policy layer and approval rules
- Run logs with replay
- Evaluation scenarios for the agent

### Delivery phases

- **Discover (1 week)**: Pick the use case, check data access and agree the pass mark.
- **Prove (2 to 4 weeks)**: Build a working pilot on your data and measure it against the pass mark.
- **Build (6 to 12 weeks)**: Production code, integrations, access control and evaluation suite.
- **Operate (Ongoing)**: Monitoring for quality, cost and drift, with regular reviews.

### Risks and controls

- **Wrong action taken**: Narrow tools, spend limits and human approval for risky steps.
- **Loops and runaway cost**: Step and budget caps per run.
- **Hard-to-audit behaviour**: Every step logged and replayable.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How much can an agent do on its own?

Only what you allow. We start with drafts and suggestions, then enable actions one at a time as measured accuracy supports it.

#### What systems can agents connect to?

Anything with an API: CRMs, help desks, ERPs, databases and internal tools. Each connection gets its own permissions.

## AI Operations (AI Ops)

> Through robust AI Operations (AIOps/MLOps), Hunexture ensures that deployed models never degrade. We implement automated monitoring, continuous retraining…

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/ai/ai-operations/

### Overview

Continuous Reliability for Machine Learning Systems. Through robust AI Operations (AIOps/MLOps), Hunexture ensures that deployed models never degrade. We implement automated monitoring, continuous retraining loops, and strict governance to treat AI with the operational maturity of enterprise software.

### What we offer

#### Continuous Monitoring & Alerting

Detecting statistical anomalies long before they impact the bottom line.

- **Data Drift Detection**: Alerting when live input data diverges from training data distributions.
- **Concept Drift Detection**: Alerting when the underlying relationship between inputs and outputs changes.
- **System Telemetry**: Tracking latency, throughput, and GPU utilization continuously.

Technologies: Evidently AI, Prometheus, Grafana

#### Automated Retraining Pipelines

Self-healing AI systems that refresh their knowledge automatically.

- **Trigger-based Execution**: Launching training jobs automatically when drift crosses a threshold.
- **Shadow Deployments**: Testing the newly trained model silently on live traffic alongside the old one.
- **A/B Testing routing**: Gradually shifting traffic to new models based on real-time ROI metrics.

Technologies: Apache Airflow, Seldon Core, Kubeflow Pipelines

#### AI Governance & Compliance

Maintaining clear line-of-sight for regulatory and ethical mandates.

- **Model Lineage Tracking**: Proving exactly what data a specific model version was trained on.
- **Bias Auditing**: Scanning training records to ensure models don’t exhibit discriminatory attributes.
- **Explainability APIs**: Generating SHAP values to explain black-box decisions to end-users.

Technologies: MLflow, Alibi Explain, AWS SageMaker Model Monitor

### Why Hunexture

- **Zero-Downtime Updates**: Hot-swapping model binaries without dropping a single API request.
- **Prevent Degradation**: We stop silent model failure that quietly leaks revenue over time.
- **Unified Dashboards**: One single pane of glass showing both technical latency and business accuracy.
- **Enterprise Readiness**: Adhering to SOC2, GDPR, and emerging AI Act compliance frameworks.

### Technologies

- **Serving**: Triton, Seldon, BentoML, TorchServe
- **Monitoring**: Evidently, Grafana, Datadog
- **Orchestration**: Kubeflow, MLflow, Airflow
- **Explainability**: SHAP, LIME, Captum

### Outcome

AI in production that stays accurate, affordable and compliant after launch.

### Best for

- Teams with models live but no monitoring
- Companies whose AI bills are growing without clear value
- Organisations preparing for audits

### Deliverables

- Quality, drift and cost dashboards
- Automated evaluation and retraining pipelines
- Incident runbooks
- Governance records

### Delivery phases

- **Baseline (1 to 2 weeks)**: Measure current quality, cost and incidents.
- **Instrument (2 to 4 weeks)**: Add tracing, evaluation and alerts.
- **Automate (4 to 8 weeks)**: Pipelines for tests, retraining and release.
- **Review (Monthly)**: Quality and cost reviews with owners.

### Risks and controls

- **Silent quality decline**: Continuous evaluation on live samples.
- **Cost creep**: Per-feature cost tracking and budget alerts.
- **Audit gaps**: Versioned models, prompts and data lineage.

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is the difference between MLOps and LLMOps?

MLOps manages trained models and data pipelines. LLMOps adds prompt versions, retrieval quality, safety tests and token cost. We cover both.

#### Can you take over a system someone else built?

Yes. We start with a review of what exists, then add monitoring before changing anything.

## Machine Learning

> At the heart of the AI revolution lies foundational Machine Learning. Hunexture excels at classic and modern ML techniques, meticulously engineering…

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/ai/machine-learning/

### Overview

Core Algorithms Driving Predictive Mathematics. At the heart of the AI revolution lies foundational Machine Learning. Hunexture excels at classic and modern ML techniques, meticulously engineering features from tabular data to unearth predictive signals that ordinary analysis misses.

### What we offer

#### Supervised Learning Frameworks

Mapping inputs to known outputs for high-accuracy predictions.

- **Regression Analysis**: Predicting continuous numerical metrics like price, age, or temperature.
- **Binary Tracking**: Detecting true/false outcomes like spam, fraud, or churn.
- **Multi-class Classification**: Categorizing inputs into complex, mutually exclusive buckets.

Technologies: XGBoost, LightGBM, scikit-learn

#### Unsupervised Learning

Finding hidden structure entirely within unlabeled datasets.

- **Customer Segmentation**: Automatically grouping clients based on latent purchasing behavior.
- **Anomaly Detection**: Flagging network intrusions or credit card fraud instantly.
- **Dimensionality Reduction**: Compressing massive datasets to visualize key driver variables.

Technologies: DBSCAN, K-Means, PCA

#### Feature Engineering Optimization

The art of mathematically transforming data before the algorithm touches it.

- **Temporal Features**: Extracting seasonality, lag, and rolling window metrics from timestamps.
- **Categorical Encoding**: Translating text categories into dense mathematical vectors.
- **Automated Feature Selection**: Algorithmically dropping useless noise data to increase model speed.

Technologies: Featuretools, Pandas, Optuna

### Why Hunexture

- **Hyperparameter Mastery**: Utilizing Bayesian optimization to squeeze every drop of accuracy out of algorithms.
- **White-box preference**: We prefer explainable tree-based models over black boxes when compliance requires it.
- **Iterative Methodology**: Rapidly testing baseline models before committing compute to massive training runs.
- **Scalable By Default**: Code built localized but designed to run distributed on Spark/Dask when data sizes explode.

### Technologies

- **Gradient Boosting**: XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost
- **Classical ML**: scikit-learn, Statsmodels
- **Distributed ML**: Spark MLlib, Dask-ML
- **Optimization**: Optuna, Hyperopt, Ray Tune

### Outcome

Models that predict, rank or classify from your data, validated honestly and deployed where they are used.

### Best for

- Forecasting demand, churn or risk
- Scoring leads, claims or transactions
- Ranking and recommendation

### Deliverables

- Feature pipeline
- Trained and validated models
- Prediction API or batch jobs
- Model card with limits

### Delivery phases

- **Discover (1 week)**: Pick the use case, check data access and agree the pass mark.
- **Prove (2 to 4 weeks)**: Build a working pilot on your data and measure it against the pass mark.
- **Build (6 to 12 weeks)**: Production code, integrations, access control and evaluation suite.
- **Operate (Ongoing)**: Monitoring for quality, cost and drift, with regular reviews.

### Risks and controls

- **Leakage that inflates accuracy**: Time-based validation and review of every feature.
- **Bias in decisions**: Subgroup testing and documented limits.
- **Models nobody trusts**: Explanations and side-by-side comparison with current practice.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How accurate will it be?

We cannot promise a number before seeing your data. The pilot measures accuracy on held-out history so you decide with evidence.

#### Do we need a data scientist on our side?

No, but a business owner who knows the process is essential. We train your team to run what we build.

## AI & ML Models

> Proprietary AI and ML models inherently constitute your most valuable intellectual property. Hunexture offers secure, isolated hosting and inferencing…

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/ai/ai-ml-models/

### Overview

Secure Hosting and Management of Foundation Models. Proprietary AI and ML models inherently constitute your most valuable intellectual property. Hunexture offers secure, isolated hosting and inferencing environments, shielding your algorithmic advantage while enabling low-latency application access.

### What we offer

#### Private LLM Deployment

Hosting massive language models entirely within your own Virtual Private Cloud.

- **Zero-Data Retention**: Guaranteeing your highly-sensitive inputs are never used to train external models.
- **Quantization & Compression**: Shrinking 70B parameter models to fit on cost-effective hardware via vLLM.
- **Custom Fine-Tuning**: Continuously updating the weights using LoRA based on your proprietary documents.

Technologies: vLLM, HuggingFace TGI, Ollama

#### Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) APIs

Wrapping your data science creations in highly robust, monetizeable API gateways.

- **High-Throughput Load Balancing**: Distributing thousands of concurrent inference requests via Triton.
- **Authentication & Throttling**: Implementing robust JWT security and rate-limiting for external customers.
- **Streaming Responses**: Deploying WebSocket connections for token-by-token realtime generation.

Technologies: FastAPI, Kong/Apigee, gRPC

#### Model Optimization & Export

Translating clunky Python models into lightning-fast compiled binaries.

- **ONNX Compilation**: Converting PyTorch or TensorFlow models to unified universal formats.
- **TensorRT Acceleration**: Merging tensor operations for massive speedups on NVIDIA hardware.
- **Edge Deployment Prep**: Converting models to CoreML or TFLite for deployment directly on iOS/Android devices.

Technologies: ONNX Runtime, NVIDIA TensorRT, TFLite

### Why Hunexture

- **Extreme Latency Focus**: We optimize inference from seconds down to milliseconds.
- **Intellectual Property Protection**: Architectures designed specifically to prevent weight extraction attacks.
- **Seamless Scalability**: Clusters that scale automatically from 0 to 100 GPUs based entirely on traffic.
- **Multi-Framework Support**: We host Scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and custom C++ models simultaneously.

### Technologies

- **Accelerated Serving**: NVIDIA Triton, vLLM, DeepSpeed
- **API Gateways**: FastAPI, Kong, AWS API Gateway
- **Model Formats**: ONNX, TensorRT, Safetensors
- **Cloud Infrastructure**: AWS Inferentia, GCP TPU, Azure GPU

### Outcome

Models hosted, versioned and served reliably, whether you run your own or use hosted APIs.

### Best for

- Teams that need private model hosting
- Products calling several models
- Companies fine-tuning for a narrow task

### Deliverables

- Model selection report with cost and quality
- Hosted endpoints or managed API gateway
- Fine-tuning pipeline where justified
- Versioning and rollback

### Delivery phases

- **Compare (1 to 2 weeks)**: Test candidate models on your task.
- **Deploy (2 to 4 weeks)**: Serve the chosen model with scaling and auth.
- **Tune (3 to 6 weeks)**: Fine-tune only if it beats prompting on your test set.
- **Operate (Ongoing)**: Version updates, monitoring and cost review.

### Risks and controls

- **Model licence limits**: Licence review before selection.
- **Latency under load**: Load testing and autoscaling.
- **Fine-tune that does not help**: Only tune after a measured gap to prompting and retrieval.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Should we fine-tune or use prompting?

Start with prompting and retrieval. Fine-tune when a measured gap remains on your test set and you have enough clean examples.

#### Can we switch models later?

Yes. We put a gateway in front so changing models is a configuration change, with tests to protect quality.

GPS trackers, OBD-II devices, phone-based driver apps and warehouse scanners. We recommend the lowest-cost option that meets your accuracy needs.

We build for Android TV, Fire TV, Apple TV, Roku and Samsung or LG TVs, usually sharing a core with the mobile apps.

Software cannot do it alone. We help you launch narrow, in one category or city, and build the tools to onboard the scarcer side first.

Stripe Connect, Razorpay Route and similar. The right one depends on your countries and model.

### Benefits

### Common challenges we solve

- Ensuring consistent service quality

- **Location privacy**: Track only while a job is active and tell users clearly.
- **Payments compliance**: Licensed processors and tax handling.

- Demand forecasting by area and hour
- ETA prediction from live conditions
- Fraud checks on accounts and promotions

### Outcomes we track

- Time to match
- Cancellation rate
- Provider utilisation

### How we work

- **01. Service Category & Matching Logic Design**: Define service categories, geographic scope, matching criteria, pricing model, and provider onboarding requirements.
- **02. Multi-sided Platform Architecture**: Two-sided marketplace architecture, real-time matching engine, payment split design, and surge pricing logic.
- **03. Provider & Customer App Development**: Consumer app, provider app, dispatcher dashboard, real-time tracking, in-app payments, and rating system development.
- **04. City Launch & Growth Operations**: Seed supply strategy, provider onboarding drive, launch city rollout, and demand-supply balancing operations support.

### Why choose Hunexture

- **Marketplace DNA**: We bring matching algorithms, dynamic pricing models and operations tooling patterns to your platform from day one.
- **Real-Time GPS Precision**: Hyper-accurate provider tracking with ETAs, route visualization, and live status updates that reduce customer anxiety and cancellations.
- **Dynamic Pricing Engine**: Surge pricing, demand-based rate adjustment, and promotional pricing rules — all configurable in real time without code changes.
- **Background Verification**: Integrated KYC, criminal background check APIs, and document verification workflows to onboard trusted providers at scale.

- Node.js

### Example scenarios (illustrative, not client results)

- **On-Demand Home Services Platform**: A platform for booking cleaning, plumbing and electrical services with provider matching.
- **Hyperlocal Food Delivery**: A food delivery app connecting restaurants, riders and customers with live tracking.
- **Home Services App**: An on-demand maintenance app with real-time booking, live tracking and payment escrow.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How does the matching algorithm work?

Our algorithm considers provider location, availability, skills, ratings, acceptance rate, and customer preferences to match the best provider in real time within seconds.

#### Can service providers set their own rates?

Yes, providers can set base rates within platform guidelines, while the system can apply dynamic surge pricing based on demand, time of day, and zone availability.

#### How do you ensure service quality?

We implement mandatory rating systems, customer reviews, background checks, automated quality monitoring, and provider deactivation thresholds to maintain high standards.

#### How does surge pricing work?

Our dynamic pricing engine automatically increases rates when demand exceeds supply in specific geofenced zones, incentivizing more providers to come online while balancing demand.

#### Do service providers need insurance?

We integrate with insurance APIs to offer providers in-app liability coverage options and can build mandatory insurance verification into the onboarding and activation flow.

#### Do you build both customer and provider apps?

Yes, plus the admin console for operations and support.

#### How do you keep maps and costs under control?

We cache and batch map requests and compare providers on cost before committing.

## Does your small business need an app, or just a better website?

> Most small businesses should start with a fast, clear website. Here is how to tell when an app is worth the extra cost and effort.

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/insights/app-or-better-website/

By Team Hunexture. Web & Apps. Published 26 November 2026. 4 minute read. Examples are illustrative, not client results.

### Start with the real question

Many owners ask us for an app. When we ask why, the answer is usually "customers should find us easily" or "we want to look serious". A website can do both.

An app is a bigger commitment. It needs design for two kinds of phones, store approvals, updates, and a reason for people to install it. So the first question is not "app or website". It is "what do my customers need to do, and how often?"

### When a better website is enough

If people visit you once in a while, they will not install anything. They will search, tap a link, read, and call or message you. A good website fits this well.

- Customers want to see what you offer, your prices or your location.
- Most enquiries come from Google or WhatsApp.
- You want bookings, enquiries or callback requests, not daily use.
- Your budget is limited and you need to start soon.

### What "better" really means

A better website is not a prettier one. It loads fast on a basic phone, says clearly what you do in the first few lines, and makes the next step obvious.

For example, a local clinic could put "Book a visit on WhatsApp" at the top of every page, list its timings, and show a map. A small change like this may help more than a new app.

- Fast on mobile data, not only on office Wi-Fi.
- One clear action on every page: call, message or book.
- Simple words. No long paragraphs about "our journey".
- Real photos, real address, real phone number.
- A WhatsApp button, because many of your customers already use it daily.

### When an app starts to make sense

An app earns its cost when people come back again and again, or when you need the phone itself.

- Customers use it often, like weekly ordering, tracking or learning.
- You need phone features such as camera, location, offline use or push alerts.
- Your staff need a tool in the field, like a delivery or service team.
- Your loyalty or subscription model depends on repeat visits.

### A middle path

You do not have to choose fully. A modern website can be added to the phone home screen, load fast, and remember a customer. This is usually cheaper than building separate apps for each phone type.

Many businesses start with a strong website, watch how customers behave for a few months, and only then decide on an app. That way the app is built on facts, not guesses.

Costs vary a lot by scope. As a rough example, a focused website usually costs well below a full app, and an app also needs yearly upkeep. We will give you a clear number after we understand your needs.

### Common mistakes we see

The same mistakes repeat, whatever the size of the business. Knowing them early saves money.

The biggest one is building for how the business looks, not for how customers behave. A feature nobody asked for is still a cost. It has to be built, tested and kept running.

- Copying a big brand's app when your customers only need a phone number and a map.
- Paying for a design that looks good but loads slowly on a basic phone.
- Skipping basics like address, timings and photos on your Google listing.
- Having no plan to update the site or app after launch.

### Questions to ask before you decide

Take ten minutes with your team and answer these honestly.

- How many times a month will one customer need it?
- Can the same thing be done with a web page and WhatsApp?
- Who will update the app and reply to store reviews?
- What happens if only a few people install it?

### How to start this week

You do not need a big plan to begin. Open your website on your own phone, on mobile data. Time how long it takes to load. Then try to book or enquire as a new customer would, and note where you get stuck.

Next, check your last twenty enquiries. How many came by call, WhatsApp, Google or walk-in? This shows where your customers already are, and that is where to invest first.

### What we'd do

We would start with the website. Make it fast, clear and easy to act on. Add WhatsApp and a simple booking or enquiry form. Then look at real visits and questions for a few months.

If people come back often, or your team needs a field tool, we would plan an app with you. If not, we will say so and save you the cost.

---

## WhatsApp automation for Indian businesses: what to automate first

> A simple order for automating WhatsApp, from instant replies to reminders, and the Meta rules you need to follow along the way.

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/insights/whatsapp-automation-what-to-automate-first/

By Team Hunexture. Automation. Published 26 November 2026. 4 minute read. Examples are illustrative, not client results.

### Why WhatsApp first

In India, many people message a business before they call or email. They ask price, timing, availability and order status. Many of these questions repeat all day.

Repeated questions are the best thing to automate. But doing everything at once usually goes wrong. Here is the order we suggest.

### Know the WhatsApp rules first

Business automation should run on the official WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API), which comes through Meta or an approved provider. Automating a personal or regular app number is risky and can get the number blocked.

Three rules shape everything. When a customer messages you, you can reply freely for 24 hours. After that window, or if you want to message first, you must use a message template that Meta has approved. And you must have the customer's opt-in before sending business-initiated messages.

- Use a number dedicated to the business.
- Ask customers before sending reminders or offers.
- Let people say "stop" and respect it.
- Expect a short setup period for business verification and template approval.
- Meta may charge for some message types, so check current rates before you plan volumes.

### 1. Instant replies and a greeting

Start small. Set up a greeting, a short menu and an after-hours message. The customer knows you got the message and what happens next.

This takes little effort. It also removes the "no one replied" problem early.

### 2. Answers to common questions

Write down the ten questions your team answers most. Prices, location, timings, delivery areas, payment options including UPI, return rules.

Turn these into ready answers. A chatbot can pick the right one, even if the customer writes in Hinglish, Hindi, Gujarati or English with spelling mistakes. Test this with real chats, because it will not be perfect.

- Use your own real answers, not generic text.
- Keep each answer short enough to read on a phone.
- Always include a way to reach a person.

### 3. Bookings, orders and enquiries

Next, let the chat collect details. For example, a salon could ask for service, date and time, then pass the booking to the owner or a calendar. A shop could take the product, quantity and address.

The goal is not to remove people. It is to get a clean, complete request so your team does not chase missing details.

### 4. Reminders and follow-ups

Once bookings and orders are flowing, add reminders. Appointment tomorrow. Payment pending. Order shipped. These can cut missed visits and many small phone calls.

These are business-initiated messages. They need an approved template and the customer's opt-in, as covered above.

### 5. Connect it to your tools

Only after the basics work, connect WhatsApp to your sheet, CRM or billing tool. Then a new lead can appear in your system without anyone copying and pasting. It can also help produce GST invoices from confirmed orders.

This is where automation can save the most hours, but it needs the earlier steps to be stable first.

### What not to automate first

Some chats should stay human, at least at the start.

- Complaints and angry customers.
- Custom quotes and price negotiation.
- Anything involving money disputes or health advice.
- Messages to people who never agreed to hear from you.

### How to know it is working

Pick two or three simple numbers before you start. How long does a customer wait for the first reply? How many chats needed a person? How many enquiries turned into bookings or orders?

Check them every week for the first month. If waiting time falls and your team spends less time on repeat questions, the setup is working. If customers keep asking for a person, the answers need work.

For example, a coaching centre could track how many admission questions the bot handled on its own, and how many it passed to staff. That is enough to guide the next improvement.

### What we'd do

We would read your last month of chats with you and list the top repeated questions. We would also set up the official WhatsApp Business Platform properly, with opt-in and templates. Then we would build steps 1 and 2 with a clear hand-off to your team.

After that we measure what customers actually do, fix gaps, and add bookings and reminders. Small steps, checked each time. If a step does not help, we stop and tell you.

## How we test AI before it talks to your customers

> AI can be wrong. This is how we test it, set limits and keep a person in the loop before an AI feature goes live for your customers.

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/insights/ai-features-you-can-trust/

By Team Hunexture. AI Quality. Published 26 November 2026. 4 minute read. Examples are illustrative, not client results.

### AI makes mistakes. Plan for it.

An AI feature can sound sure and still be wrong. It can make up a price, misread a question, or answer something it should not. This is normal behaviour for these models, not a rare bug.

So the job is not to find a perfect model. The job is to build a system around it that catches mistakes before they reach your customer. We use three tools: evals, guardrails and human review.

### Evals: a test set before launch

An eval is a list of real questions with the answers we expect. We run the AI against the list and check how often it gets them right. Think of it as an exam.

We build the list with you, from your real chats, forms or documents. We include hard and tricky cases, not only easy ones.

- We run the exam before launch and again after every change.
- If a change makes results worse, we do not ship it.
- We keep adding to the list as new cases appear.

### Guardrails: clear limits

Guardrails are rules around the AI. They decide what it may do and what it must refuse.

For example, a support assistant for a shop could be limited to answer only from the shop's own product and policy pages. If the answer is not there, it says so and offers a person.

- Answer only from approved sources.
- Refuse topics outside the job, such as medical or legal advice.
- Keep private customer data out of answers.
- Check outputs for format and risky content before sending.
- Limit actions, like refunds, to small safe steps.

### Human review: a person for the risky parts

Some decisions should not be left to AI alone. We decide with you which ones. Usually these are money, contracts, complaints and anything hard to undo.

In those cases the AI prepares a draft and a person approves it. If the test results show the AI is reliable on a task, we can reduce review for that task. Not before.

### A small example

Take a support assistant for an online shop. A customer asks, "Is this available in blue, and when will it reach Pune?"

Without limits, the AI may guess. With this setup, it looks up stock and delivery rules from the shop's own data. If it cannot find a clear answer, it says so and hands the chat to a person.

Evals check this exact kind of question before launch, and review checks a sample after. The customer gets a fast answer or a fast hand-off. Either is better than a confident wrong reply.

### Watching it after launch

Launch is the start. Real customers ask things nobody planned for. We keep logs, with privacy in mind, and review a sample regularly.

We also set up a simple way to flag a bad answer, and a fallback to a person. If something goes wrong, the system should fail safely, not quietly.

- Track wrong answers and hand-offs to people.
- Review a sample each week at first.
- Update the test list from real mistakes.
- Keep a switch to turn the feature off fast.

### Be honest about limits

We will not promise 100 percent accuracy. No one honest can. We will tell you what the AI is good at, where it struggles, and what we do about it.

If a task needs certainty, such as exact calculations, we use normal software for that part and let AI handle the language part.

### Questions to ask any AI vendor

Whoever builds your AI feature, including us, should answer these in plain words.

- How do you test it before launch, and can I see the results?
- What is it not allowed to do?
- When does a person step in?
- Where does my customer data go, and who can see it?
- How do I switch it off if something goes wrong?

### What we'd do

We would pick one narrow task and build the test list with you first. Then we add limits and a review step for anything risky. We launch to a small group, watch the results, and widen only when the results hold up.

You see the test results at each step, in plain language, so the decision to go further is yours.

## Chatbot or AI agent? Picking the right level of automation

> A chatbot answers. An agent acts. Here is how to choose the simplest option that does the job, and when plain automation is enough.

Canonical URL: https://hunexture.com/insights/chatbot-or-ai-agent/

By Team Hunexture. AI & Automation. Published 26 November 2026. 4 minute read. Examples are illustrative, not client results.

### Two words, two different jobs

People use "chatbot" and "AI agent" as if they mean the same thing. They do not. The difference matters for cost, risk and results.

A chatbot talks. It answers questions and collects details. An agent does work. It can look things up, use your tools and take several steps to finish a task.

### What a chatbot is good at

A chatbot is the right choice when the job is mostly questions and answers.

- Answering common questions about products, timing and policies.
- Collecting name, phone and need, then passing it to your team.
- Guiding a customer through a fixed set of choices.
- Working on your website or WhatsApp, day and night.

### What an agent adds

An agent can do more than reply. It can check an order in your system, update a record, or draft an email and ask for approval, all in one flow.

For example, an agent for a small distributor could read an incoming order message, check stock in a sheet, prepare a draft invoice and ask the owner to confirm. A chatbot alone could only take the message.

- It connects to your tools such as sheets, CRM or billing.
- It can take several steps toward one goal.
- It decides what to do next based on what it finds.

### The cost of more power

More power means more that can go wrong. An agent that can change records can also change them wrongly. It needs more testing, tighter limits and often a person to approve key steps.

It also takes longer to build and costs more to run. That is fine when the saved time is large. It is wasteful when a simple chatbot would do.

### A simple way to choose

Ask these questions about the task you want to automate.

- Is it only answering and collecting details? Choose a chatbot.
- Does it need to look up or change data in your systems? Consider an agent.
- Is a mistake costly or hard to undo? Add human approval, whatever you pick.
- Are the steps always the same? Plain automation may be cheaper than both.

### Two quick examples

A chatbot case: a dental clinic could use a chatbot to answer timing and fee questions, and collect a name and preferred slot. The front desk then confirms. Simple, safe and useful.

An agent case: a small logistics firm could use an agent that reads a customer's "where is my parcel?" message, checks the tracking sheet, and replies with the status. If the parcel is delayed, it drafts an apology and asks a staff member to approve it.

Each is a good fit for its own job. Neither would suit the other.

### Do not skip the boring parts

Whatever you choose, a few basics decide if it works. Your information must be correct and up to date. Your tools must have clean data. And there must be a clear way to reach a person.

If your price list is out of date, a chatbot will repeat the wrong price faster than a person. Fix the source first, then automate.

- Keep one trusted source for prices and policies.
- Test with real customer questions, not only ideal ones.
- Decide who owns the system after launch.

### You can grow into it

The best path is often to start with a chatbot and add abilities one by one. First it answers. Then it books. Then it checks stock. Then it drafts documents for approval.

Each step is tested before the next. You get value early, and you do not pay for power you do not use.

### What we'd do

We would sit with you and walk through one real task from start to finish. We note every question, every system and every decision involved.

If a chatbot covers it, we build a chatbot. If not, we build the smallest agent that can do the job, with limits and approval where it matters. We would rather say "you do not need an agent yet" than sell you one.
